sessionTitle: Microsoft Dataverse plugin: unleashing coding agents on the enterprise

announcements.name: Dataverse plugin for coding agents
announcements.shortDescription: A single capability embedded in existing coding tools that turns business intent into governed Dataverse operations across schemas, data, queries, security, and admin tasks.
announcements.longDescription: The Dataverse Skills plugin is a single capability embedded in the coding tools a team already uses that turns plain-English business intent into governed Dataverse operations spanning schemas, data, queries, security, and admin operations, all without leaving the workflow. The session demonstrates three different roles doing three different jobs with this single approach, starting with Maya [inferred], a builder who installs the plugin, connects via her Microsoft sign-in, and from one prompt has the agent discover her environment, configure the MCP server, and verify the connection. No config files, docs, setup, or guides are required.

announcements.name: Identity-based environment discovery
announcements.shortDescription: The agent discovers the user's Dataverse environment from their Microsoft sign-in and configures the MCP server, requiring no org URL, config files, or setup docs.
announcements.longDescription: Because Maya [inferred] doesn't know her org URL and shouldn't have to, she connects using her Microsoft sign-in and issues a prompt asking the agent to connect her to her Dataverse environment. The agent discovers her environment from her Microsoft identity, configures the MCP server, and verifies the connection, all from one prompt with no pasted URL, config files, docs, setup, or guides. This lets her then describe and build a full data model in business terms.

announcements.name: Skill-based execution with on-demand tooling
announcements.shortDescription: Plugin skills such as DBQuery and DVData encode best-practice knowledge and generate tools on the fly, using the Python SDK behind the scenes to parse Excel files and run generated scripts.
announcements.longDescription: The Dataverse plugin for coding agents has skills that encode best-practice knowledge of how to address a particular use case or task, including the ability to use tools behind the scenes such as the Python SDK and to generate on-demand tools that achieve the user's requirements. In the demo this lets the agent parse real Excel files (not CSVs) from a reference data folder and import them into the newly created tables, resolving lookups via business keys rather than GUIDs and reporting any failures. Kent notes it behaved more like a data pipeline than a sample generator, handling lookup dependencies correctly.

announcements.name: Inline security simulation
announcements.shortDescription: The agent validates a security model by simulating each user's access and returning a pass/fail table, replacing manual private-browser impersonation.
announcements.longDescription: To validate a security model without juggling multiple browser sessions, Amara issues a prompt to validate the security model for each of Dakota, Lisa, and Mario, simulating their access and reporting whether they can read an account record, see a lifetime value, read a roast batch record, and read each other's business unit records, returned as a clear pass-fail table. The agent runs all 15 security validation tests inline and they pass, showing green check marks and red X's where each is expected. This replaces the usual manual process of logging in as each user in a private browser tab, confirming the configuration in seconds.
